vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: soul-in-sapphire
Version: 1.0.8

The 'soul-in-sapphire' skill bundle is a comprehensive framework for managing an agent's long-term memory and emotional state using Notion. It utilizes a sibling skill, 'notion-api-automation', via controlled shell execution (execFileSync) to interact with the Notion API. The scripts (e.g., emostate_tick.js, ltm_write.js, setup_ltm.js) are well-documented and align strictly with the stated purpose of persisting memory, tracking identity shifts, and generating daily journals. No evidence of data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, obfuscation, or malicious prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's code, declared requirements, and runtime instructions are coherent with a Notion-backed long-term memory / emotion/state tracker and only ask for a Notion API key and node — nothing unrelated or disproportionate was found.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the actual files and behavior: scripts read a local config, create/query Notion databases, write journal/state/emotion records, and perform LTM writes/search. Required binaries (node) and primary env var (NOTION_API_KEY) are appropriate for Notion API use.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the agent to run the included node scripts and to use a sibling 'notion-api-automation' notionctl helper (or an override via NOTIONCTL_PATH). Scripts read/write the local config (~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json) and may read files passed to identity_diff/conflict_track. They do not contact unknown external endpoints directly; all external I/O goes through the Notion API via notionctl as declared. One minor scope mismatch: README and some scripts reference a subagent payload builder dependency (subagent-spawn-command-builder), but the SKILL.md metadata only lists 'notion-api-automation' as a dependency.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no download/install spec — the skill is delivered as scripts and docs that run on node. No remote installs or archive downloads were found. The code does call execFileSync to run a local notionctl script; this is expected and uses a sibling skill or explicit NOTIONCTL_PATH rather than fetching remote code at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only NOTION_API_KEY is required (declared as primaryEnv). An optional NOTIONCTL_PATH is supported to override the helper script path. The skill reads and writes a local config under ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire which is appropriate for storing Notion DB IDs. No unrelated credentials or broad environment access were requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable. It writes its own config into ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire which is reasonable. The code can produce subagent payloads (subagent_spawn_plan.js and references to spawn profiles) and delegates payload generation to other builder skills — you should review those pieces if you plan to allow autonomous invocation, but autonomous invocation alone is normal and not flagged here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a Notion-backed LTM and emotion/state/journal system. Before installing or enabling autonomous use, do the following: 1) Protect your NOTION_API_KEY (store it in environment or secret store); revoke it if you uninstall. 2) Install or verify the notion-api-automation skill (or set NOTIONCTL_PATH) because the scripts call a local notionctl helper; otherwise commands will fail. 3) The README mentions an additional dependency (subagent-spawn-command-builder) that is not listed in SKILL.md metadata — if you intend to use subagent features, install and audit that builder skill. 4) The skill reads/writes ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json and will create Notion DBs during setup — ensure you are comfortable giving the integration access to the workspace and that the DB schemas are acceptable. 5) If you will allow the agent to invoke this skill autonomously, review the subagent-related scripts (subagent_spawn_plan.js and any omitted files) to ensure they don't spawn agents or execute actions you don't want. Otherwise the package is internally consistent and proportionate to its stated purpose.
